stem.en: The Egyptian year had 12 months of 30 days plus 5 extra days, 365 days in all. Why did it slowly slip behind the seasons?

text.en: The months were of unequal length.

feedback.en: All 12 months had 30 days, so the months were equal, and 5 extra days were added at the end.

text.en: The Nile flood came at a different time each year.

feedback.en: The flood could vary from year to year, but that would not push the calendar steadily in one direction.

text.en: Sirius rose at a different time each year.

feedback.en: Sirius was what the Egyptians watched to fix the year. The fault was in counting 365 days, not in the star.

text.en: The real year is about a quarter of a day longer than 365 days.

explanation.en: The real year is about 365 and a quarter days, so a calendar of exactly 365 days falls one day behind every four years, and 30 days behind in 120 years.

hints.en: Compare 365 with the true length of a year.
